title: Exact counterexamples and stable oscillations in a two-host dormancy model
oneLine: An exact parameter family overturns a proposed coexistence-convergence claim, and a certified local Hopf bifurcation creates attracting cycles.
abstract: This unrefereed mathematical candidate gives an explicit one-parameter counterexample family in a six-dimensional two-host dormancy–infection model. Both resident equilibria resist within-resident perturbations and can be invaded, yet the unique coexistence equilibrium is unstable. Every nonnegative equilibrium is hyperbolic, and almost every strictly positive trajectory fails to converge to an equilibrium. A separate dormancy-parameter calculation certifies a supercritical Hopf bifurcation and stable small periodic orbits locally beyond its threshold. This is a deterministic model result, not empirical validation or a proof that almost every trajectory becomes periodic.

keyResults: An explicit admissible family for every C ≥ 1/2 has a unique positive coexistence equilibrium with two unstable directions.
Both resident equilibria are stable within their resident subsystems and invasible by the other host.
Almost every strictly positive trajectory fails to converge to any equilibrium.
A certified supercritical Hopf bifurcation near q = 0.9769161486 gives stable small cycles locally on its upper side.

narration: Dormancy can sustain oscillations. An Evidence Press briefing. In a mathematical model of two competing hosts and a virus, one host can enter a dormant state. A proposed convergence claim suggested that, under particular coexistence conditions, the populations should settle to a steady balance. This candidate constructs an exact family where that conclusion fails. Both single-host resident states can be invaded by the other host, but the unique coexistence state is unstable. Almost every strictly positive starting state fails to approach any equilibrium. That does not, by itself, say what those trajectories eventually do. A separate calculation varies the dormancy probability and locates a Hopf bifurcation near zero point nine seven six nine one six. Immediately beyond that boundary, the proof guarantees small, stable periodic oscillations. It does not certify a whole range of larger cycles, or say that almost every trajectory becomes periodic. The distinction matters: failure to settle at an equilibrium is weaker than a complete description of the long-term dynamics. The evidence package combines a self-contained mathematical argument, exact algebra, and integer-based interval calculations checking the local bifurcation. Numerical pictures are not the proof. This is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed research candidate about a deterministic model, not an empirical finding about biological populations. Internal checks are not external peer review or independent reproduction. Released on 18 October 2026, the paper and reproducible evidence are linked on the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.
